learningObjective: Choose the narrowest safe recovery scope by testing whether ranks share one proven training state before retrying, rebuilding a group, or rolling back.
mediumRationale: A compact Mermaid decision flow is the smallest medium that separates failure detection from recovery authorization and makes the state-consistency gate control every safe path. Labelled branches preserve the conditional logic without implying quantitative relationships.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Selected: the lesson is a decision graph with explicit evidence gates, recovery branches, and a single return to training; automatic layout keeps that relational structure maintainable.
mediumComparison.svg: Rejected: the learning task is conditional rather than geometric or quantitative, so hand-positioned paths would duplicate Mermaid graph semantics without adding explanatory value.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Rejected: a table could compare failure classes and remedies, but it would not show that the same consistency proof must precede every narrow recovery decision.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected: a failure-scenario chooser would add controls and hidden states when all safe branches fit in one static flow.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected: the reviewed sources verify runtime and recovery semantics but do not provide this article-specific decision flow. No source figure, layout, wording, data, or code is reused.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected: the prose lists failure types and remedies well, but readers can still pair a visible symptom directly with a retry. The missing mental model is that recovery scope follows state evidence, not symptom category alone.

pages.insight: The preceding ML-design slide covers data validation, metrics, and system requirements but contains no distributed-training failure or recovery model.

The training checklist recommends checkpointing the model object, train/validation/test data, and hyperparameter configuration for reproducibility, but does not address sharded completeness, integrity, atomic publication, or recovery scope.
The neighboring worked system-design slide moves to a personalized-feed example and adds no checkpoint or failure semantics.
The slide immediately before the distributed-training material discusses data pipelines, privacy, and bias; it adds no runtime fault-tolerance guidance.

The distributed-training slide distinguishes data and model parallelism and mentions gradient checkpointing for memory, but does not discuss process failure, collectives, consistent recovery state, or persistent checkpoints.
The following production-serving slide covers model gates, updates, inference, and interpretability rather than training failure recovery.
The Rules of ML slide says to watch for silent failures, but it concerns production ML pipelines and provides no silent-corruption detector or distributed recovery contract.
The algorithms-and-data-structures divider ends the relevant ML-production neighborhood and contains no fault-tolerance material.

sources.title: torchrun (Elastic Launch)
sources.usage: Used as official runtime documentation to verify that one worker failure stops and restarts the worker group, and that elastic membership changes form a new worker group with new rank and world-size assignments.

sourceReview.notes: The hardest mental model is that a timeout, slow rank, checksum mismatch, or process exit is evidence of a problem but not permission to retry locally. A narrow recovery is safe only when participating ranks can prove agreement on the committed step and all trajectory-defining state, and when the operation is idempotent or membership change is explicitly supported. Otherwise the affected consistency domain must roll back to a complete, integrity-checked checkpoint; an incomplete candidate must be rejected. The visual deliberately says 'affected consistency domain' rather than always 'whole job' because data-parallel replicas may sometimes have valid isolation boundaries while tensor, pipeline, or optimizer-sharded groups often do not.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, searched all 214 deck pages and inspected both relevant neighborhoods, then checked two official PyTorch references, NVIDIA NCCL communicator semantics, and a primary LLM fault-tolerance paper before selecting an original recovery-evidence decision flow.

implementation.accessibility: The Mermaid source provides a complete accessible title and description. Decision diamonds, explicit yes/no edge labels, direct state labels, and solid versus dashed paths carry the logic without color. The compact top-to-bottom flow uses established theme-aware primitives, remains readable at 390 CSS pixels, and resets through shared Mermaid print behavior.
